rubrics.justification: The response appropriately notes the limitations of a single static image, describes a blastocyst that may be partially collapsed/re-expanding, and avoids overcalling ICM/TE quality. It is broadly consistent with the image, though somewhat generic and not highly precise about visible zona thinning or exact expansion.
It thoroughly integrates age, ovarian reserve, oocyte yield, BMI, semen parameters, endometrial thickness, prior cycle history, and fresh-transfer context with embryo quality to frame prognosis.

The reasoning is logical and internally consistent: strong prognosis is supported by young age and favorable embryo/patient factors, while uncertainty from untested status and fresh-cycle receptivity is appropriately acknowledged.

Recommendations are well aligned with standard IVF practice, especially favoring eSET in a young good-prognosis patient and not over-investigating after one failed transfer. Minor limitation is that some counseling points are broader clinical advice rather than explicit guideline-based distinctions.
It provides clear practical next steps for transfer management, luteal support, OHSS monitoring, eSET, and future planning including when to escalate evaluation after failure.
